analysis:
Examined .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py. The base excerpt covers lines 1084-1404 and the head excerpt covers lines 1-565. The patch adds offline unit tests at head lines 949-982. Those lines fall outside the visible head unit and are known only from the patch excerpt.

The new tests assert three behaviors:
- A GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT=2 rerun hands off with MANUAL_SCAN_RERUN_DISABLED, makes no paid calls and never clears.
- The scanner runtime bound defaults to 900s, accepts 3000s and rejects invalid values.
- A workload-call ceiling stops at the unadmitted stage with BEDROCK_WORKLOAD_LIMIT.

This is CI review-tooling test code only. It has no interaction with the provider/coordinator assets, boundaries or threats (A-001..A-017, TB-002..TB-011, T-041 etc.). No production code, endpoints, crypto, attestation, cache or billing paths of the darkbloom provider are touched.

The tests use synthetic tokens and localhost HTTP fixtures. They print no secrets and assert diagnostics omit private payloads. Fail-closed semantics are tested, not weakened.

The implementation of runtime_seconds, rerun handling and the workload policy in threat-model-review.py and threat_review/* is not in this batch. Their correctness is outside the supplied evidence. That is a coverage limit only, not a provider threat-model concern.

No regression to the provider threat model was identified.
